title: Restoration of the intervertebral disc as a living load-bearing organ

concept.text: The innovation would restore a degenerated intervertebral disc as a durable living organ whose tissues work together to support spinal movement and loading. Its scope includes the hydrated central nucleus, the surrounding annulus, and the endplates that interface with the vertebrae. Success would require recovery of their coupled biological and mechanical functions, including disc height, internal pressure, containment, and appropriate motion-segment stiffness. The supplied human evidence does not demonstrate that integrated capability.

The biological aim is to rebuild tissue that maintains its own functional matrix under everyday loading. Aggrecan and other matrix components retain water, producing osmotic pressure that helps the disc resist axial compression; that pressure must operate within a competent surrounding structure. Symptom relief or an increase in disc volume could be useful intermediate results, but neither alone establishes restoration of this living load-bearing system.

significance.text: Durable restoration would provide a biological treatment option for appropriately selected patients with disc-driven disease who might otherwise require surgery. Fusion stabilizes a spinal segment by eliminating motion, while artificial disc replacement provides a prosthetic alternative. Neither returns the patient's degenerated disc to a living, hydrated organ. By restoring the disc's own structure and function, this innovation could preserve motion and physiological load sharing; whether it actually reduces surgery or improves outcomes relative to existing treatments would require comparative clinical evidence.

The immediate advance would be structural and biomechanical, with clinical benefit requiring separate demonstration. Disc degeneration and back pain do not have a simple one-to-one relationship, and the reviewed literature identifies other pain generators, including facet arthropathy. Restoring a disc would therefore not establish a cure for all back pain or guarantee that every treated patient avoids fusion.

Conditional implications and limits: if restoration proved safe, durable, and clinically effective, it could shift treatment of selected degenerative discs toward biological preservation and potentially defer more invasive reconstruction. Coexisting facet disease, stenosis, and centralized pain could still require other treatment. These are boundaries on the proposed capability and possible downstream consequences, not outcomes established by the supplied trials.

missing_breakthrough.text: The central unsolved capability is integrated human restoration: rebuilding the nucleus, annulus, and endplate together while recovering disc height, hydration, pressure, and functional mechanics. In the supplied clinical evidence, cell therapies have not demonstrated that combination. This is a conclusion about the reviewed record, not proof that every possible human result has been excluded or that the field remained unchanged through November 1, 2026.

The adult disc is largely avascular, has limited nutrient supply, and operates under continuous mechanical loading. Degeneration adds a hostile environment characterized in the review by low oxygen, acidity, and high osmolarity. A regenerative treatment must sustain viable, functional cells and matrix production under those conditions. Findings in preclinical models do not by themselves show that a treatment can overcome the nutritional, chemical, and mechanical constraints of a degenerated human disc.

Engineering synthesis: the tissues must recover compatible functions together. Restoring water retention and pressure requires an annulus capable of containing the nucleus and endplates capable of supporting the restored organ's function. The treatment must maintain that coordination through repeated loading rather than produce only a temporary imaging change. A further barrier is measurement: convincing human evidence must connect tissue repair to mechanical function using validated, acceptably safe methods.

current_state.text: Ferraz and colleagues synthesized clinical evidence through May 7, 2025 in North American Spine Society Journal, volume 25, article 100841, DOI 10.1016/j.xnsj.2025.100841. They described 13 trials of low to moderate quality showing modest, statistically significant improvements in pain and disability without persuasive imaging evidence of biological repair. Their assessment supports a gap between symptomatic improvement and demonstrated human regeneration. It does not establish that cell therapies have no clinical effects or that future whole-disc restoration is impossible.

The supplied review assessed Ferraz's full article through an alternative full-text XML artifact, with no reported truncation or extraction problems. It nevertheless identified apparent study-classification and reference mismatches in the article's tables, which reduce confidence in aspects of its synthesis without negating the separately reviewed trial findings. The earlier December 20, 2025 publication date is unverified: the artifact contains differing date fields, including December 19, 2025 and January 28, 2026, whose roles were not resolved.

Beall and colleagues randomized 404 adults with chronic low back pain and moderate degenerative disc disease. The trial's primary efficacy endpoint did not reach statistical significance for either cell-treatment group versus control in the overall study population, although some additional pain analyses favored treatment. Published online March 31, 2025 in The Spine Journal, volume 25, pages 1997–2013, DOI 10.1016/j.spinee.2025.03.015, this study illustrates why a failed primary endpoint and favorable additional analyses must both be retained. Neither finding establishes integrated disc regeneration. The supplied assessment relied on the PubMed abstract record rather than inspected full trial reporting.

Gornet and colleagues reported a randomized phase I/II study of allogeneic disc progenitor cells involving 60 participants, including 20 high-dose recipients. The high-dose group had a reported mean disc-volume increase of 249 mm³ at 52 weeks and pain improvement; the vehicle group also experienced significant pain improvement. Published July 4, 2024 in the International Journal of Spine Surgery, DOI 10.14444/8609, the study disclosed sponsor-related financial interests and research funding. The volume finding is a structural signal, but it does not by itself establish superiority over controls, recovery of disc pressure, or restoration of the complete motion segment. Financial relationships are relevant context rather than proof that the result is invalid.

For Gornet's study, the supplied review retained abstract material, captions, and disclosures, without full methods or inspected images. The saved PubMed pages had no reported extraction problems, but complete extraction of an abstract record does not provide the evidentiary coverage of a full paper. These access limits constrain interpretation of both trials. The supplied freshness record is empty, and the documented literature-search cutoff is May 7, 2025; retrieval of the supplied artifacts on November 1, 2026 does not establish comprehensive coverage of developments through that date.

completion_criteria.text: Proposed demonstration: in symptomatic lumbar discs with moderate degeneration, a treatment would restore disc height, hydration, internal pressure, annulus integrity, endplate competence, and motion-segment stiffness to prospectively specified healthy reference ranges appropriate to spinal level and patient characteristics. Adjacent discs should not automatically define normality because they may also be degenerated or mechanically different. These are proposed criteria for testing this innovation, not established consensus standards.
completion_criteria.label: Restore integrated disc function to prospectively specified healthy reference ranges

completion_criteria.text: Proposed durability and clinical test: a randomized comparison would show maintenance of the structural and mechanical gains for at least five years, together with meaningful patient benefit, acceptable safety, and reduced need for fusion at the treated level. Five years is a proposed durability threshold. Pain improvement alone would not satisfy the whole-organ objective, while structural improvement without meaningful clinical benefit would leave practical usefulness unresolved.
completion_criteria.label: Randomized five-year durability with meaningful benefit, safety, and reduced fusion

completion_criteria.text: Proposed verification and reproducibility: measurement methods, reference ranges, clinically important differences, safety limits, and handling of subsequent surgery would be specified before the study. Assessment should distinguish biological repair from changes in volume alone and use validated, acceptably safe measurements or proxies for mechanical function. Independent replication across centers and patient groups would establish demonstrated breadth. Initial success in moderate lumbar degeneration would not establish effectiveness in advanced collapse, other spinal levels, or every source of back pain.
completion_criteria.label: Prespecified verification methods and independent replication across centers and populations

related_concepts.text: Roster-based synthesis: ORT-02, Biological restoration of the osteoarthritic synovial joint, shares the goal of restoring a coupled living load-bearing system. ORT-04, Regeneration of the load-bearing tendon–bone enthesis, similarly requires functional integration across tissues and interfaces. ORT-05 remains distinct because its target is the nucleus–annulus–endplate system and its hydration, pressure, and spinal mechanics.

Roster-based synthesis: ORT-09, Regeneration of a functioning growth plate, and ORT-10, Single-episode restoration of segmental long bone by vascularized, remodelable bone, also concern organized skeletal tissues with specific functional roles. Growth-plate regeneration aims to recover growth function; segmental bone restoration explicitly requires vascularized, remodelable bone. Disc restoration must address the largely avascular disc environment and recover disc mechanics, so success in either neighboring concept would not establish ORT-05.

Roster-based synthesis: ORT-01, Adult epimorphic regeneration of a functional limb, spans coordinated regeneration at a larger anatomical scale. ORT-06, Force-bearing skeletal muscle after volumetric muscle loss, and ORT-07, Meaningful motor and sensory recovery across long peripheral-nerve gaps, share the requirement that anatomical repair produce useful function. Their principal targets are muscle force and neural recovery, respectively; neither substitutes for restoration of disc load bearing.

Roster-based synthesis: ORT-08, Anatomically precise and reversible control of osteogenesis, concerns where and how bone forms rather than restoration of a disc's hydrated tissues. ORT-03, Eradication of mature biofilm in bone and on orthopedic implants without removing the reconstruction, concerns infection clearance while preserving an existing reconstruction. Such capabilities could matter in particular orthopedic settings, but they remain separate from biological disc regeneration.

unresolved_issues: The supplied record does not establish comprehensive developments after the May 7, 2025 literature-search cutoff through November 1, 2026.
Ferraz's exact publication chronology remains unresolved because the supplied artifact contains differing date fields.
The extent to which Ferraz's apparent study-classification and reference mismatches affect its aggregate conclusions remains unresolved.
Full trial methods, complete comparative structural analyses, and relevant images were not inspected in the supplied assessment of the Beall and Gornet studies.
Validated, acceptably safe methods and numerical thresholds for demonstrating restored human disc pressure, endplate competence, and integrated motion-segment mechanics remain to be specified.
The proposed five-year durability threshold, suitable patient-selection boundaries, and achievable reduction in subsequent fusion require prospective justification and testing.

brief.title: Living spinal discs that bear weight again
possible: People with a damaged spinal disc could regain living tissue that supports weight and allows movement. Its water-rich center, containing outer ring and surfaces joining it to the bones would work together again. The repaired disc would maintain its own tissue under everyday loads.
why: For selected people whose disc damage causes symptoms, this could offer a biological alternative to surgery. Restoring the disc’s own function could preserve movement and natural load sharing. Spinal fusion holds bones together by stopping movement; artificial discs replace tissue with a device.

sources.showed: Their review found modest improvements in pain and disability across 13 trials of low to moderate quality, without convincing imaging evidence of tissue repair.
sources.quote: Clinical evidence, however, is limited: thirteen low to moderate-quality trials show modest, albeit statistically significant, improvements in pain and disability, without compelling imaging proof of biological repair.
sources.cited_for: Symptom relief has outpaced convincing evidence of human disc regeneration.
sources.not_established: The trials do not demonstrate a restored living disc whose tissues bear loads together.

sources.showed: A randomized trial in 404 adults missed its main test of treatment success for both cell treatments versus control. Some additional pain analyses favored treatment.
sources.quote: The primary efficacy endpoint for the trial did not reach significance for either treatment group compared to control in all subjects.
sources.cited_for: A large controlled trial gave mixed results for treating symptoms with injected cells.
sources.not_established: The trial does not establish whole-disc repair or recovery of coordinated mechanical function.

sources.showed: In a small randomized trial, the group receiving a high dose of donor disc cells had increased disc volume and less pain. The injection carrier alone also reduced pain.
sources.quote: High-dose allogeneic disc progenitor cells produced statistically significant, clinically meaningful improvements in back pain and disc volume at 1 year following a single intradiscal injection and were safe and well tolerated.
sources.cited_for: Injected disc cells have produced a human signal of structural change.
sources.not_established: Greater volume alone does not establish superiority over controls, restored internal pressure or a functioning spinal joint.

shown: Gornet and colleagues have reported increased disc volume alongside pain improvement in a small human trial. This is a step toward structural repair, but nobody has yet demonstrated restoration of the disc’s center, outer ring and bone interfaces as a coordinated living system.
missing: Human treatment has yet to restore disc height, water content, pressure, containment and movement mechanics together.
Repair must keep cells alive and producing tissue despite scarce nutrients, acidity and repeated loading.
Human studies must connect tissue repair to mechanical recovery using validated measurements that are acceptably safe.

milestones.label: Disc structure and mechanics return to healthy ranges
milestones.explanation: Moderately damaged lower-back discs would regain healthy height, hydration, pressure, outer-ring integrity, bone-interface function and joint stiffness against suitable preset ranges. This would establish coordinated restoration.

milestones.label: Five-year repair brings benefit, safety and fewer fusions
milestones.explanation: A randomized comparison would show lasting structural and mechanical gains for five years, meaningful patient benefit, acceptable safety and fewer treated-level fusions. This would establish durable clinical usefulness.

milestones.label: Independent teams reproduce results using predefined measures
milestones.explanation: Studies would preset validated measures, healthy ranges, benefit and safety thresholds, and handling of later surgery, with independent replication across centers and patient groups. This would establish reproducibility and breadth.

uncertain: Healthy reference ranges and safe ways to measure restored pressure, bone-interface function and joint mechanics still need agreement.
The proposed five-year threshold, suitable patient groups and achievable reduction in fusion need testing.
Disc damage and pain do not map directly onto each other, so successful repair may leave other causes of back pain untreated.

page.title: Intervertebral disc regeneration
page.definition: Living disc tissue again bears physiological loads at a degenerated level of the human spine, through repair of the existing disc or integration of a living tissue-engineered replacement. The fibrous outer ring (annulus fibrosus) contains the water-rich core (nucleus pulposus). Together with the cartilage endplates adjoining the vertebrae, they transmit pressure and permit movement.

goal.need: Low back pain affected 619 million people in 2020, and about 90% of cases have no identifiable specific cause. In one study of 92 patients with chronic low back pain, testing reproduced the usual pain at an abnormal disc in 36, with a negative control. Medicines can ease symptoms, and spinal fusion stops motion at the treated level. For people whose pain persists despite conservative care and comes from a degenerating disc, repair could provide lasting relief while preserving movement there.

figures.caption: The burden of low back pain exceeds the population identifiable for disc-specific treatment.
figures.note: Neither figure estimates how many people have pain attributable to a disc or could receive regenerative treatment.

statements.quote: alleviation of pain, stabilization or restoration of structure, and normalization of biomechanical function.
statements.context: The recommendations identify these as the three principal efficacy objectives for biological disc regeneration therapies.

completion.title: Human disc regeneration restores living tissue, physiological mechanics and relief of disc-related pain.
completion.criterion: A controlled human study demonstrates living repair of the nucleus, annulus and endplate interfaces, recovery of physiological load-bearing and motion, and alleviation of disc-related pain. Tissue repair and mechanical recovery must be demonstrated in the same treated discs through direct measurements or validated, clinically justified surrogates. Success criteria must be specified prospectively. Pain relief or increased disc volume alone does not satisfy this conjunction.
completion.set_by: Atlas provisional criterion, derived from the ORS efficacy objectives; no outside body identified defines an integrated human whole-disc completion test.
completion.basis: Searches of ORS recommendations, ISSLS consensus, FDA spinal guidance, ASTM recognition records and registered disc-cell protocols found no integrated human regeneration threshold. ORS supplies the pain–structure–mechanics objectives. FDA spinal guidance concerns implant evaluation; ASTM F2346 concerns nonbiologic artificial discs and supplies no performance standard. The provisional test adds no numerical tolerance or fixed follow-up duration.

milestones.title: A living disc restores tissue structure and mechanical function in a small-animal spine.
milestones.criterion: Demonstrate new disc matrix, preservation or restoration of disc structure, and recovery of mechanical function in a small-animal spine. Compare the treated level with native discs using structural measurements and mechanical testing.
milestones.set_by: ORS Spine Section, Smith et al., sections 6.1–6.2 and Figure 1; qualitative efficacy objectives applied at the small-animal proof-of-concept stage.

milestones.title: A living disc recovers structure and mechanical function in a large-animal spine.
milestones.criterion: Demonstrate structural repair in a large-animal spine and mechanical recovery toward native-disc function. Apply load to the treated motion segment, including the disc and adjacent vertebrae, and compare its mechanical response with that of native segments.
milestones.set_by: ORS Spine Section, Smith et al., sections 6.1–6.2 and Figure 1; qualitative efficacy objectives applied at the large-animal stage.

milestones.title: A disc regeneration cell therapy is administered to patients in an FDA-authorized phase 1 study.
milestones.criterion: At least one patient receives the investigational disc cell therapy in a phase 1 study, including the phase 1 component of a combined phase 1/2 study, under an FDA Investigational New Drug application in effect.
milestones.set_by: US Food and Drug Administration, clinical research phases and Investigational New Drug process; applicable here to investigational cell products.

milestones.title: Rexlemestrocel-L beats saline on the combined response at both 12 and 24 months.
milestones.criterion: For rexlemestrocel-L alone or with hyaluronic acid, the posterior probability that the response rate exceeds the saline response rate must be greater than 0.9875. A responder has both a reduction from baseline of at least 50% in average low back pain over the previous 24 hours on a visual analogue scale and a decrease of at least 15 points on the 100-point Oswestry Disability Index at both 12 and 24 months, with no adjudicated post-treatment intervention at the treated level through month 24.
milestones.set_by: Mesoblast, MSB-DR003/NCT02412735 protocol, version 7.0 dated 17 December 2018; the threshold was written for lumbar mesenchymal precursor-cell treatment.
milestones.threshold_quote: required a posterior probability of superiority >0.9875

milestones.title: A controlled human study demonstrates disc tissue repair alongside clinical benefit.
milestones.criterion: Meet the registered primary clinical efficacy endpoint and demonstrate biological tissue repair in the treated discs against a control group. A change in disc size or water content requires evidence linking that change to repair of living tissue.
milestones.set_by: Atlas provisional criterion combining the ORS structural objective with controlled clinical benefit. RESPINE defines paired clinical and hydration outcomes. No external criterion identified requires both clinical success and evidence of living tissue repair.

milestones.title: Delivered stem cells survive, differentiate and secrete matrix in a cultured disc explant.
milestones.criterion: Deliver the candidate cells into excised disc tissue maintained in culture. Identify the delivered cells in the tissue and demonstrate their viability, differentiation toward a disc cell phenotype and deposition of disc matrix.
milestones.set_by: California Institute for Regenerative Medicine, Discovery Inception Award DISC1-10643, explant objective
milestones.threshold_quote: To optimize stem cell delivery, survival, differentiation and matrix secretion in an intervertebral disc (IVD) explant

milestones.title: A disc repair treatment supports viable cells and disc matrix production in culture.
milestones.criterion: Demonstrate cell viability and the proposed regenerative activity in a culture relevant to the target disc tissue. For a treatment intended to rebuild nucleus matrix, assess production of matrix constituents such as aggrecan and type II collagen.
milestones.set_by: Disc regeneration preclinical testing convention described by Thorpe et al., sections 2–2.2, and the ORS Spine Section, section 6.2
milestones.threshold_quote: This stage is used to perform initial proof of principle studies and fundamental cellular toxicology (viability) studies on relevant cell types.

milestones.title: Disc cell therapy improves clinical response and MRI-measured disc hydration versus sham at 12 months.
milestones.criterion: Compare intradiscal allogeneic bone marrow stromal cells with sham on both RESPINE co-primary outcomes at 12 months. A clinical responder has a decrease in pain of at least 20% and at least 20 mm on the visual analogue scale, or a reduction of at least 20% on the Oswestry Disability Index. Assess increased fluid content in the affected disc using the ratio of the month-12 value to baseline on sagittal T2-weighted MRI. The protocol gives no minimum percentage gain in hydration.
milestones.set_by: University Hospital of Montpellier, RESPINE protocol 9766, EudraCT 2017-002092-25, sections E.2.1 and E.5.1
milestones.threshold_quote: The change in fluid content is expressed as the ratio of fluid content at month 12 vs fluid content at baseline.

not_found: No external numerical completion threshold for integrated human disc regeneration was found in the reviewed ORS, ISSLS, FDA, ASTM or trial documents.
No external combined human tissue-repair and clinical-benefit success criterion was identified.
Validated human pass/fail ranges for restored intradiscal pressure, endplate function and motion-segment mechanics were not identified.

results.finding: Mesenchymal precursor cells with or without hyaluronic acid (404 patients) fell short of the 0.9875 composite superiority threshold versus saline.
results.detail: The abstract gives no arm-specific posterior probabilities.
results.quote: The primary efficacy endpoint for the trial did not reach significance for either treatment group compared to control in all subjects.

results.finding: Mesenchymal precursor cells plus hyaluronic acid reduced mean low back pain versus saline through 24 months in a 404-patient trial.
results.quote: While the primary and secondary responder efficacy endpoints were not reached, MPC+HA significantly reduced LS mean LBP compared to control at 12 and 24 months in all subjects.

results.finding: An FDA-approved Phase I/II disc progenitor-cell trial enrolled 60 patients and reported outcomes after intradiscal cell injection.
results.detail: The supplied abstract gives enrollment and treatment results for the combined study.
results.quote: Sixty patients with symptomatic single-level lumbar degenerative disc disease (mean age 37.9 years, 60% men) were enrolled in a randomized, double-blinded, placebo-controlled Phase I/Phase II study at 13 clinical sites.

results.finding: High-dose disc progenitor cells (20 assigned) produced a 62.8% mean reduction in VAS back pain at week 52.
results.detail: The vehicle arm also improved from baseline. The abstract reports no direct between-group efficacy comparison or biological validation of the volume increase.
results.quote:
At week 52, the high-dose group had a mean VAS percentage decrease from baseline (-62.8%,
P
= 0.0005), achieving the endpoint of back pain improvement >30%; the mean change was also significantly greater than the minimal clinically important difference of a 20-point decrease (-42.8,
P
= 0.001).

results.finding: Goat disc constructs showed proteoglycan and collagen staining after 13 weeks in culture. The preimplantation histology sample size was unreported.
results.detail: The paper reports nucleus aggrecan and type II collagen staining after implantation.
results.quote: Alcian blue (proteoglycans) and picrosirius red (collagen) stained sections of the eDAPS prior to implantation (after 13 weeks of pre-culture).

results.finding: Rat caudal disc implants recovered near-native segment compression at 20 weeks (n = 6 treated segments tested).
results.detail: External fixation retained the implants during healing. At harvest, tensile moduli were within the native range, while failure stress reached 46.6% of the native value.
results.quote: Results from this study show that the eDAPS mature compositionally over time in vivo in the rat tail, achieving mechanical properties that are similar to the native disc at 20 weeks.

results.finding: Goat cervical disc replacements approached native motion-segment compression at 8 weeks (n = 3 treated segments tested).
results.detail: The anterior plate stabilized the segment during healing. Testing after its removal measured axial compression ex vivo. Unfixed in vivo load-bearing and long-term motion remained unmeasured.
results.quote: eDAPS moduli and strains were not significantly different from the native cervical disc after 8 weeks in vivo.

results.finding: Ovine marrow stem cells pooled from 3 donors deposited glycosaminoglycan-rich matrix in 21-day pellet culture.
results.detail: The pellet assay characterized the cells used for injection. It did not test their effect on resident disc cells in culture.
results.quote:
Isolation of total RNA and qRT‐PCR demonstrated
COL2A1
and
ACAN
gene expression, and the presence of toluidine blue stained GAG in pellet sections (Figure
2
B).

results.finding: Stem cell-treated sheep discs in the established cohort had greater lateral bending stiffness than saline controls (n=6 per group, P<0.05).
results.detail: Testing used bending and rotation without axial compression. Lateral bending stiffness remained below native levels, and the neutral zone remained larger than in native segments.
results.quote:
MSC treatment caused an increase in stiffness in the lateral direction compared to PBS injected IVDs (
P
< 0.05) and this was reduced compared to NOC IVDs (
P
< 0.05).

results.finding: Human stem cell-derived disc organoids (n = 3 experiments/group) showed increased nucleus-region aggrecan and type II collagen staining at day 28.
results.detail: Viability was measured separately in the component hydrogels using live/dead staining.
results.quote:
The organoid group also exhibited more COL2- and
ACAN-positive staining in the NP region and more COL1-positive staining
in the AF region

results.finding: After lumbar discectomy in goats (n = 12 total), organoid-treated motion segments had a compressive modulus closer to native and higher than discectomy alone (P < 0.01).
results.detail: The mechanical result covers compression at the six-week endpoint. Long-term performance under cyclic and shear loading remained untested.
results.quote:
The organoid-implanted
motion segments exhibited a compressive modulus significantly restored
toward native levels, confirming successful mechanical integration
and load-sharing.

results.finding: Among 23 patients followed at 42 months, mean Pfirrmann grade fell by 0.65 after allogeneic stromal cell injection.
results.detail: The reported MRI significance tests compare each group with its own baseline. The clinical follow-up reports pain and disability separately.
results.quote:
Thus, 
from baseline to 42 months, the Pfirrmann grading signifi-
cantly increased in the controls by 1.0 (baseline, 3.15; 42 
mo, 4.16; Figure 1E), whereas for the MSC-treated patients, 
there was a significant decrease of >0.6 (baseline, 3.59; 42 
mo, 2.94; Figure  1F).

results.finding: Goat stromal cell–seeded engineered discs showed proteoglycan staining after 13–15 weeks of preimplantation culture (culture control n unreported).
results.detail: The precultured constructs served as matrix-staining controls for the implantation study.
results.quote: Alcian blue and picrosirius red stained histology sections demonstrated that fixed and remobilized eDAPS were compositionally similar, with reduced alcian blue staining compared to pre-implantation eDAPS or the native goat cervical disc

results.finding: Goat cervical engineered discs (n=7 mechanically tested) had 2× native toe and linear compressive moduli in the remobilized group.
results.detail: Compression testing included four remobilized and three continuously fixed goats. Transition and maximum strains showed no detectable group differences. Range of motion was modeled.
results.quote: with a significant doubling of toe and linear region compressive moduli compared to native in the remobilized group

results.finding: Autologous bone marrow stromal cells versus sham (46 patients at follow-up): treated disc height index reached 105.1% of baseline at six months.
results.detail: Six-month MRI was available for 18 cell-therapy and 23 sham participants. The authors identified injected fluid volume as a possible contributor to increased disc height.
results.quote:
In the BM- MSC group, DHI (Figure  3B) significantly increased 
at 3 months (103.5 ± 5.1%, p = 0.023 vs. baseline) and 6 months 
(105.1 ± 6.8%, p = 0.017 vs. baseline)

results.finding: In the AMG0103 trial (25 adults), disc height increased by 0.31 mm in the high-dose group at 12 months.
results.detail: The text gives the total sample and the placebo group size but does not state the size of the high-dose group.
results.quote: Further, disc height declined by 0.25 mm at 12 months for the placebo group, while the 10 mg AMG0103 cohort disc height increased by 0.31 mm over the same period.

results.finding: After lumbar discectomy, acellular UPAL gel (n=40) yielded lower MRI Pfirrmann degeneration grades than discectomy alone (n=34) at both follow-ups (P < 0.01 each).
results.detail: MRI follow-up was at 24 and 96 weeks, with 26 UPAL and 24 control patients completing 96-week follow-up. Between-group tests used unadjusted P values. The study collected neither disc histology nor local biomarkers.
results.quote: MRI revealed that the disc degeneration score was significantly lower in IVDs with UPAL implantation than in those that underwent discectomy alone.

results.finding: Human mesenchymal stem cells from 2 donors remained viable through 4 weeks in bovine nucleus pulposus explants (n=16 injected), acquired disc markers and deposited local matrix.
results.detail: Sox-9 staining was transient. Matrix deposition was assessed qualitatively by extracellular immunostaining near the labelled cells.
results.quote: MSCs were identified in all injected tissue samples and cell viability was maintained for the 4 weeks investigated. MSCs displayed cellular staining for Sox-9, and displayed cellular and matrix staining for aggrecan and type II collagen that increased during culture.

results.finding: In bovine nucleus pulposus explants (n=3 per time point), injected human mesenchymal stem cells survived and showed disc-like differentiation and matrix deposition through 6 weeks.
results.detail: The authors attributed matrix in the cells-only arm to the injected cells based on its localization to their clusters. In the hydrogel arm, infiltrating native cells could also have contributed to the deposited matrix.
results.quote:
Immunopositive cellular and matrix staining
for collagen type II, aggrecan and chondroitin sulphate was observed
within the vicinity of the cell clusters where hMSCs had been
injected alone, from 48 h to 6 weeks in culture ( Fig. 6 ).

results.finding: All 15 enrolled patients received NuQu juvenile chondrocytes in a Phase I study under US IND BB-IND 13985.
results.quote: Fifteen patients were treated with a single percutaneous delivery of NuQu juvenile chondrocytes.

results.finding: In RESPINE (114 randomized), intradiscal allogeneic bone marrow stromal cells had a 5.25-percentage-point higher clinical response rate than sham at 12 months.
results.detail: Table 3 shows increased hydration in 11/29 cell-treated patients (37.93%) and 10/24 sham patients (41.67%). MRI data were available for 55 patients, and 53 were analyzed after two withdrew consent.
results.quote: At 12 months after the intervention, the percentage of responders was 74% of patients in the experimental group vs 68.8% in the placebo group ( table 2 ).

results.finding: In 121 adults with lumbar discogenic pain, intradiscal nucleus pulposus allograft exceeded sham on the primary pain responder endpoint by 58.4 percentage points.
results.detail: The 6-month analysis carried forward earlier observations for 56 of 61 sham participants, including 55 who crossed over at 3 months. The trial included no follow-up imaging or biomechanical outcomes.
results.quote: The prespecified 6-month primary endpoint, analyzed with LOCF for the 55 sham participants who crossed over, was met: back pain MCID responder rates were 60.0% (36 of 60) in the allograft group and 1.6% (1 of 61) in the sham group (difference 58.4 percentage points, 95% CI 43.9 to 69.9;

results.finding: Human nucleus pulposus cells in HA-pNIPAM hydrogel (n = 3 per condition) showed approximately 95% viability in both loaded and unloaded cultures.
results.detail: The Results report 21 days of construct culture, while parts of the Methods describe 14 days.
results.quote:
LIVE/
DEAD analysis revealed approximately 95 % NP cell 
viability in both loaded and unloaded conditions (Fig. 
5a,c).

definition = "Living disc tissue again bears physiological loads at a degenerated level of the human spine, through repair of the existing disc or integration of a living tissue-engineered replacement. The fibrous outer ring (annulus fibrosus) contains the water-rich core (nucleus pulposus). Together with the cartilage endplates adjoining the vertebrae, they transmit pressure and permit movement.". Reason: The definition leaves unclear why an integrated living disc replacement counts among the animal results.

goal.need = "Low back pain affected 619 million people in 2020, and about 90% of cases have no identifiable specific cause. In one study of 92 patients with chronic low back pain, testing reproduced the usual pain at an abnormal disc in 36, with a negative control. Medicines can ease symptoms, and spinal fusion stops motion at the treated level. For people whose pain persists despite conservative care and comes from a degenerating disc, repair could provide lasting relief while preserving movement there.". Reason: The existing paragraph gives the burden of all low back pain but omits the patient group, the limits of current treatment and the benefit of preserving motion.

add statement by National Institute of Arthritis and Musculoskeletal and Skin Diseases, 2007: "The repair and regeneration of cartilage, meniscus, tendon, ligament, and intervertebral disc are especially difficult". Reason: The 2007 funding notice identifies disc regeneration among the repair problems addressed by the NIAMS Bioengineering Research Partnerships programme.

add statement by iPSpine consortium, EU Horizon 2020, 2025: "regenerative treatment of IDD, restoring the IVD to a functional unit.". Reason: The iPSpine report supplies an explicit funded project objective linking disc regeneration to recovery of function.

add milestone after None: "Delivered stem cells survive, differentiate and secrete matrix in a cultured disc explant.". Reason: The disc explant stage tests whether cells survive and make matrix after delivery into tissue, a question that isolated cell culture cannot settle.

add milestone after None: "A disc repair treatment supports viable cells and disc matrix production in culture.". Reason: The first proof-of-principle stage tests biological activity and cell viability in culture before progressing to intact tissue or a spine.

edit m1: criterion = "Demonstrate new disc matrix, preservation or restoration of disc structure, and recovery of mechanical function in a small-animal spine. Compare the treated level with native discs using structural measurements and mechanical testing.". Reason: The rat study's sample sizes, follow-up and findings obscure the reusable small-animal test.

edit m2: criterion = "Demonstrate structural repair in a large-animal spine and mechanical recovery toward native-disc function. Apply load to the treated motion segment, including the disc and adjacent vertebrae, and compare its mechanical response with that of native segments.". Reason: The goat study's fixation, loading cycles and observed differences are features of one experiment rather than requirements for large-animal evidence.

edit m3: criterion = "At least one patient receives the investigational disc cell therapy in a phase 1 study, including the phase 1 component of a combined phase 1/2 study, under an FDA Investigational New Drug application in effect.". Reason: The criterion needs actual human administration in the phase named in the title, while the published allocation counts belong with the result.

edit m4: title = "Rexlemestrocel-L beats saline on the combined response at both 12 and 24 months."; criterion = "For rexlemestrocel-L alone or with hyaluronic acid, the posterior probability that the response rate exceeds the saline response rate must be greater than 0.9875. A responder has both a reduction from baseline of at least 50% in average low back pain over the previous 24 hours on a visual analogue scale and a decrease of at least 15 points on the 100-point Oswestry Disability Index at both 12 and 24 months, with no adjudicated post-treatment intervention at the treated level through month 24."; threshold_quote = "required a posterior probability of superiority >0.9875"; threshold_ref = 27; refs = [7, 27, 12]. Reason: The revision specifies the sponsor's strict posterior-probability cutoff, the interval for interventions and the distinction between an individual response and superiority of a treatment arm.

add milestone after m4: "Disc cell therapy improves clinical response and MRI-measured disc hydration versus sham at 12 months.". Reason: RESPINE supplies a registered human benchmark pairing clinical response with a quantitative structural measure before the stronger test of living tissue repair.

edit m5: criterion = "Meet the registered primary clinical efficacy endpoint and demonstrate biological tissue repair in the treated discs against a control group. A change in disc size or water content requires evidence linking that change to repair of living tissue."; set_by = "Atlas provisional criterion combining the ORS structural objective with controlled clinical benefit. RESPINE defines paired clinical and hydration outcomes. No external criterion identified requires both clinical success and evidence of living tissue repair."; refs = [2, 4, 11, 28]. Reason: The existing criterion mixes a within-group volume result with the stronger requirement for controlled evidence of living tissue repair.
remove not found 3. Reason: The Ferraz full text is available in PubMed Central and the Gornet full text in the journal PDF, making the combined access note obsolete.

remove statement 2. Reason: VERTEBRA defines how investigators should report evidence for a regeneration claim, so its statement belongs with the evidence criteria rather than among declarations of a therapeutic goal.
remove statement 1. Reason: The undated NIAMS quotation covers musculoskeletal tissues generally, while its dated research notice explicitly names the intervertebral disc.
